news.content:
President Donald Trump urged data center developers on Wednesday to pay host communities a "dividend," as AI-driven projects draw opposition from voters across the political spectrum.

In a Truth Social post, Trump said projects that were highly unpopular in some areas became "extremely popular" once a financial deal was struck.

“If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a "dividend." I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck,” Trump wrote.

Trump first floated the idea in late September, saying residents could receive dividends or teacher bonuses. "Now people are going to benefit directly," he said.

Backlash crosses party lines

Data centers powering artificial intelligence (AI) have become a political flashpoint nationwide. Opposition now unites voters across ideological lines.

A September Fox News survey found 71% of registered voters oppose building an AI-related data center in their area. Data centers have become a key issue for Republicans.

Trump says on-site power can lower bills

Trump has previously also argued data centers can ease electricity costs. He said new facilities must generate their own power, which he argued could lower prices.

U.S. tech companies’ data center lease commitments topped $850 billion in the first quarter. Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) led at about $250 billion, followed by Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) at about $197 billion and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) at about $183 billion.

news.author: Namrata Sen
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) has surpassed 10 million downloads with its Muse AI agent, adding momentum to the company’s AI push as U.S. downloads for OpenAI’s ChatGPT weaken.

Muse recorded 10.9 million downloads since its September launch. New data from Sensor Tower showed that over 10.2 million downloads came from the U.S., indicating strong early domestic adoption for Meta’s AI product, Yahoo Finance reported on Tuesday.

Only 11 other applications have exceeded 10 million U.S. downloads within 40 days, according to the data. Meta’s Threads was the most recent example, reaching that benchmark in July 2023.

Sensor Tower estimated that Muse surpassed 2.5 million daily active users for the first time on October 16, with users rising 15% week over week in the prior seven-day period.

By comparison, U.S. downloads for OpenAI’s ChatGPT dropped 25% during the latest 30-day period compared with the previous 30 days, the report noted.

Meta and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.

Read Also: Meta Platforms, Tesla Could Swing More Than $100 Billion After Earnings

Muse Faces Revenue Hopes

Muse’s rapid adoption arrives as the company is set to announce its third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, after the bell.

Earlier this month, a Deutsche Bank analyst said Muse could eventually account for as much as 8% of Meta’s revenue by 2030, as per Yahoo Finance.

During Meta’s July second-quarter earnings call, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said personal AI agents would underpin the company’s next phase of product development and monetization.

“We are developing new personal agents that will be the foundation for our next wave of products and revenue lines in the months and years ahead,” Zuckerberg said.

Privacy Concerns Mount Over Chat Links

The product, however, also faces scrutiny over data-sharing controls. On Tuesday, Meta suspended Muse’s conversation-sharing feature after security researchers said public domain name system (DNS) records could expose thousands of shared chat links.

Researchers at Claroc said Muse generated predictable sharing URLs that incorporated conversation titles into web addresses under a common domain structure. The researchers reported that about 6,800 chats were exposed.

Price Action: On a year-to-date basis, Meta stock climbed 5.18%, as per Benzinga Pro. In Wednesday’s pre-market session, it traded 0.28% lower at $692.30.

news.author: Tanya Rawat
news.content:
Market commentator The Kobeissi Letter said U.S. electricity prices are "skyrocketing," with the average residential price up 11% since January 2025 to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, near an all-time high.

The Kobeissi Letter made the remarks in a post on X, linking the rise to the AI boom.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene separately posted on X that "AI companies are claiming they are going to pay Americans thousands for free every month."

Power Prices Climb As AI Demand Surges

The Kobeissi Letter said average prices in the first eight months of 2026 were 40% higher than in the same period of 2019. Maine saw the largest increase at 90%, followed by California and New York at nearly 70%.

The analysis noted that data centers need "enormous amounts of electricity" to power thousands of chips and cooling systems, and that a 1-gigawatt data center can consume as much electricity as 800,000 homes. Wholesale prices in areas near significant data center activity surged by as much as 267% between 2020 and 2025.

"The AI revolution is driving a surge in electricity demand, and households are increasingly feeling the cost," the post read.

Greene Warns On AI ‘Living Wage’ Claims

Greene wrote that AI companies are claiming the payments will come every month as a "living wage" and that "you won’t need to work." She added: "Kids, nothing is free in life."

Washington Weighs Who Pays

The posts come as the fight over who covers data center power costs plays out in Washington. Last month, the House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3, which would require utilities to consider rates for certain large-load customers that recover the cost of upgrading the grid to serve them.

The Trump administration also launched a voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT), Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ: META), Oracle Corp. (NYSE: ORCL), OpenAI, xAI, and Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) agreed to cover grid upgrades tied to their data centers.

Separately, Vice President JD Vance defended the Trump administration’s data center expansion, acknowledging that facilities can "cause real problems" and calling residents’ reported $300 electricity bill increases "totally unacceptable."

news.author: Radhika Anilkumar Nadig
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) wants Muse to be the artificial intelligence agent people run their lives through. A decade from now, the winner may be whoever customers trust with their payments, and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) are in that race too.

Trust Beats the Model

Technology analyst Luke Lango and Futurum Chief Market Strategist Shay Boloor told Benzinga the AI model may be the “least durable advantage” because capability is converging and costs keep falling.

Lango, the editor of Innovation Investor, said the lasting edge belongs to the agent people trust “with their card and their habits.” Boloor said it would be “memory and trust accumulated over years.”

Meanwhile, Muse has passed 10.9 million downloads since its September debut, including 10.2 million in the U.S., according to Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch. Only 11 other apps have reached 10 million U.S. downloads within 40 days.

U.S. seven-day retention was 30%, compared with an average of 19% for rivals including OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s Grok.

Apple and Amazon Face Different Tests

Lango said Apple is “quietly well-placed” because it has the device, the wallet, and consumers’ trust.

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan sees a risk, as Apple “can keep every handset sale and still lose discovery, referral, and transaction initiation” to Muse. He said Siri has yet to match Muse on background tasks, third-party actions, and payments.

Amazon has gone the other way. It blocked Muse from its site while Shopify Inc. and PayPal Holdings Inc. signed on.

Lango believes Amazon is most at risk if the wall stays up after consumers start shopping through agents.

One Default Agent, and Room for a New Giant

The analysts expect the market to settle on one default agent, built into the phone, browser or messaging app and free or bundled for most users.

Lango does not think consumers will pay for several of them and the rest will become features.

That does not mean the incumbents win by default.

Boloor said he would be surprised if the shift to AI agents did not “create new winners”, and Lango named OpenAI as a candidate for a new giant, even though he said incumbents are better placed because they own distribution and can afford the capital spending.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said earlier this month that he is prepared to spend up to $200 billion on AI to “really lead in the area for decades to come.”

Shares of artificial intelligence (AI) hardware companies, cloud providers, and cryptocurrency miners gained in pre-market trading after Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO Elon Musk stated there is no available AI compute capacity on the market.

Musk Confirms Compute Shortage

During SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call, Musk highlighted a severe shortage of AI compute resources across the industry. Musk said, “We are also frankly hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler and by dozens of smaller companies to rent more of our compute.”

He noted the sheer volume of interest the company is receiving for its infrastructure. Musk added that SpaceX could rent out its compute “several times over if we said yes to everyone.”

Read Also: Top Analyst Says SpaceX, Super Micro's Blowout Results Delivered the Catalyst for Next AI Stock Rally: ‘Odds Based on History Are High’

Cloud Providers Have ‘No Cheese’

Musk explained that SpaceX attempted to rent inference compute from other cloud providers to free up their own internal capacity for model training, but found no hardware available to rent.

Comparing the situation to a comedy sketch where a cheese shop has no cheese, Musk noted that inquiries for older and newer chips, including H100s, newer generation chips, and custom silicon like Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs, were met with the same response: “Nope, don’t have any of those.”

Musk concluded his market assessment by stating, “Yeah, so I don’t think we’re going to have a demand issue here.”

Neoclouds and Miners Rally

Following Musk’s comments, related infrastructure and hardware stocks saw positive movement before the market opened. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) showed a pre-market gain of 2.17% and Neocloud providers like CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) and Nebius Holdings NV (NASDAQ:NBIS) also rose, posting pre-market increases of 2.35% and 2.26%, respectively.

Cryptocurrency miners, which often operate as alternative data centers for AI workloads, traded higher as well. IREN gained 4.02% in the pre-market.

Editor’s Note: This story has been updated to include NVIDIA stock’s Wednesday premarket movement.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) rose nearly 2% in Wednesday premarket on news that Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO Elon Musk expects to bring thousands of Nvidia chips online every month through year-end, which Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman said shows the chipmaker’s projections playing out.

SpaceX Is Bringing 200,000 Nvidia GPUs Online

Musk said on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday that the company is “tracking to be able to bring roughly 200,000” Nvidia GB300s online per month for the rest of the year, with next year “primarily Vera Rubin compute.”

It is “absolutely insane” to supply the power and cooling to turn on 220,000 GB300s a month, he said, “but that is actually what we’re doing right now, and that pace will obviously accelerate next year.”

He is “fairly confident” of adding an incremental 10 gigawatts of compute in 2027, and said SpaceX plans a 440,000-chip Vera Rubin training cluster by the end of the second quarter.

Read Also: SpaceX, Netflix, Super Micro Computer, Tesla and Meta: Why These 5 Stocks Are on Investors' Radars Today

Analysts React to Nvidia’s Move

Newman said on X that Nvidia was “ripping on news that what it has said would happen is in fact happening.”

Earlier this Month, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that new chip orders are arriving “almost weekly and daily,” with customers asking for more supply.

Futurum’s Shay Boloor said the pace means about 600,000 GPUs in the fourth quarter from SpaceX alone.

SpaceX Spending Ramps With the Buildout

Musk said earlier this year that the company will use Nvidia hardware exclusively to build its data centers. It is also reportedly seeking about $40 billion in loans and debt, led by Apollo Global Management Inc., to buy Nvidia chips, Reuters reported, citing the Financial Times.

SpaceX’s third-quarter revenue came in at $14.58 billion, beating estimates of $12.74 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. It reported earnings of 35 cents per share beat estimates of 12 cents.

Nokia Corporation (NYSE:NOK) shares are in the spotlight, with earnings on deck, AI and Cloud demand in focus, a new AI-RAN partnership with Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI), a technical setup showing a trend in repair mode and Edge Rankings all drawing attention.

  • Nokia stock is surging to new heights today. What’s fueling NOK momentum?

Earnings Preview & History

Nokia is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on October 22 before the market opens. Analysts estimate earnings per share of 8 cents along with revenue of $5.80 billion. For the prior quarter, Nokia reported earnings per share of 8 cents, beating the consensus estimate of 7 cents. The company also posted revenue of $5.60 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $5.59 billion.

What to Watch: AI Demand, Outlook & Cash Flow

Investors will be closely tracking AI and Cloud demand. Sales to AI and Cloud customers more than doubled in the second quarter and order intake was EUR 2.8 billion, with Nokia expecting about half of those orders to convert to revenue over the next 12 months. Full-year guidance will also be in focus. Nokia expects comparable operating profit of EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 2.6 billion, tracking somewhat above the midpoint, and Network Infrastructure sales growth of 12% to 14%.

Cash flow will draw attention as well, after free cash flow was negative EUR 0.7 billion in the second quarter and management said it expects to track toward the low end of its 55% to 75% conversion target. So will the effect of rising memory chip prices on margins.

Super Micro and Nokia Partner on AI-RAN Using Nvidia’s Aerial RAN Computer Platform

Super Micro announced a partnership with Nokia to deploy AI-RAN, which combines Nokia’s radio access network technology with the NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)‘s Aerial RAN Computer platform and Supermicro’s AI-optimized infrastructure. The approach puts accelerated compute inside the radio network, so operators can run radio and AI workloads on the same infrastructure. Targeted uses include voice AI, vision AI, physical AI and autonomous network operations. Supermicro’s systems span distributed cell sites, aggregation locations and core network hubs, and the companies describe the setup as a software-driven path toward 6G.

Supermicro’s servers for the platform are generally available now, and a two-unit system with dual Nvidia Vera processors is on display at Nvidia GTC Berlin, Oct. 20-22, and will be available later this year. A second system is planned for customer testing later this year, with general availability in the first half of 2027.

A Trend in Repair Mode, With a Golden Cross From 2025 Still Intact

Even with Wednesday’s premarket bounce, Nokia is still trading below its major trend gauges: about 7.5% below the 20-day SMA ($10.07), 8.9% below the 50-day SMA ($10.22), and 17% below the 100-day SMA ($11.22). That keeps the intermediate trend in "repair mode," with rallies needing follow-through to reclaim the $10 area where multiple averages cluster.

Momentum is best framed through MACD right now: MACD is below its signal line and the histogram is negative, which points to upside pressure fading versus the prior upswing unless buyers can push it back above that baseline. Zooming out, the 20-day SMA remains below the 50-day SMA (a bearish alignment), but the longer-term picture still has a constructive marker from the golden cross that formed in October 2025 (50-day SMA above the 200-day SMA).

Recent turning points help explain the current range: the stock logged a swing low in August, then a swing high in September, and it previously broke below support in March—so traders are watching whether this bounce is just a counter-trend move or the start of a more durable base. From a longer lens, the 52-week range ($5.45 to $17.45) shows the stock is well off its June peak, which is why overhead supply can show up quickly on rallies.

  • Key Resistance: $11.00 — a round-number area that lines up with the stock’s gap to the 100-day SMA ($11.22), making it a natural "prove it" zone for rebounds
  • Key Support: $8.00 — a nearby round-number floor that sits above the 52-week low ($5.45), where dip-buyers may look to defend if momentum rolls over again

Benzinga Edge Rankings

Below is the Benzinga Edge scorecard for Nokia, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses compared to the broader market:

  • Momentum: Bullish (Score: 80.41) — The stock’s trend profile is strong versus the broader market, even if it’s still working through overhead resistance.
  • Quality: Neutral (Score: 37.07) — Fundamentals screen as mixed, suggesting execution and margins remain important swing factors.
  • Value: Neutral (Score: 50.28) — Valuation looks closer to the middle of the pack on this model, rather than a clear bargain or extreme premium.
  • Growth: Neutral (Score: 45.8) — Growth characteristics are moderate, so the next catalyst likely hinges on guidance and demand commentary.

The Verdict: Nokia’s Benzinga Edge signal reveals a momentum-led profile, with the strongest pillar coming from trend strength rather than deep value or high growth. With earnings one day away, traders may treat $11.00 as the key upside "reclaim" level, while $8.00 is the nearby line in the sand if the post-report reaction turns volatile.

President Donald Trump mandated that new data centers generate their own electricity, as BlackRock Inc. (NYSE:BLK) CEO Larry Fink stated that slowing data center construction will increase inflation.

Trump’s Power Generation Mandate

On Wednesday, President Trump said on Truth Social that he wants data center developers to produce their own power. “New and large, in some cases gigantic, data centers are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid,” Trump stated.

To counter local opposition to these facilities, Trump suggested companies offer financial incentives to residents. “If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a dividend,” Trump noted.

He added that facilities facing opposition become popular when financial agreements are reached, concluding, “Make Deals, and get them built!”

Read Also: Trump Says Communities Hosting AI Data Centers Could Get a ‘Dividend' From Teacher Bonuses to Payments: 'People are Going to Benefit Directly'

Fink’s Economic Warnings

Simultaneously, BlackRock CEO Fink warned that obstructing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure expansion carries economic risks.

Speaking to Bloomberg Television, Fink linked construction delays directly to rising prices. “If we don’t build out these data centers, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now,” Fink said.

He added that a slowdown in the build-out of this technology could “jeopardize the economy.”

Fink also addressed the broader economic impact in a separate CNBC interview. “If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession,” Fink said.

Wall Street analysts estimate that total AI capital expenditures could exceed $5 trillion by 2030, according to CNBC.

Fink noted that local opposition is often based on “misinformation” and emphasized the economic benefits of the industry.

“Data centers are not the problem. They’re creating more new jobs than ever before,” Fink stated, adding that the investment creates demand for construction workers and energy infrastructure.

How Has the Stock Market Performed?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 12.45% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 13.73%, and the Dow Jones gained 8.50% YTD.

On Tuesday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed mixed. SPY rose 0.34% to $769.05, while QQQ declined 0.10% to $717.63. Meanwhile, the Dow tracker, State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), ended 1.05% higher at $524.36.

In premarket trading on Wednesday, SPY was up 0.25%, QQQ rose 0.62%, and DIA advanced by 0.44%.

news.content:
For three weeks, the market treated every artificial intelligence hardware stock as guilty until proven innocent.

On Wednesday, the verdict came from an unexpected witness: a rocket company.

AI Hardware Stocks Rebound After SpaceX’s Blowout Results

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) rose 7.3% in premarket trading after its third-quarter report showed its AI business turning profitable.

Chip, server and memory stocks rallied in its wake, from Seoul to New York.

Over the past month, 26 of the largest U.S.-listed AI hardware stocks lost roughly $1.6 trillion in combined market value, according to Benzinga calculations based on TradingView data.

Wednesday’s premarket gains put back about $274 billion, or roughly 17% of what was lost.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index closed Tuesday 14.6% below its Oct. 6 close. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) rose 1.6% before the bell.

Read Also: Are Companies Reducing AI Spending? Chip Orders Say Otherwise

What SpaceX Actually Reported

SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from a year earlier, against expectations of $12.7 billion.

The surprise came from its superintelligence segment, which includes a cloud business renting AI computing power to companies such as Anthropic.

Segment revenue nearly tripled to $7.56 billion, and it swung to an operating profit of $431 million from a $1.26 billion loss in the second quarter.

“We could rent out our compute several times over if we said yes to everyone,” CEO Elon Musk said on the earnings call.

Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen said new data centers pay for themselves in less than a year at current prices.

The selloff was built on fear that AI spending would never pay back.

Super Micro Gives the Rally a Second Engine

Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) jumped 11.2% in premarket trading after an upbeat sales outlook and better-than-expected margins.

If it holds, it would be the stock’s biggest one-day gain since Aug. 12.

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) rose 5.1%, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (NYSE:HPE) gained 4.4% and Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE:VRT) added 5.1%.

Amkor Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:AMKR) climbed 8.2% after Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) said the chip packager will expand advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028.

Read Also: AI's Most Watched Cooling Stock Has Fallen for 11 Straight Days: Analysts Now See a 50% Upside

Seoul Moved First

South Korea’s KOSPI rose 3.3% on Wednesday. SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) gained 5.8% and Samsung Electronics Co. (OTC:SSNLF) rose 5.7%.

“All the signs suggest that traders are prepared to buy the dip once again,” David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said in a note.

One Good Day Is Not a Bottom

The semiconductor index snapped an eight-session losing streak on Monday.

LPL Financial’s Adam Turnquist found the index has fallen at least seven straight sessions only 16 times since 1994. Three-month gains after those streaks averaged 9.5%.

“History suggests that this alone is not an all-clear signal,” Turnquist said.

The Rebound Has a Long Way to Go

CoreWeave would need to rise about 40% to recover its one-month loss, and Intel about 31%.

Even after its premarket jump, SpaceX trades about 21% below its record close of $201.80, set on June 16.

Tonight Decides Whether the Witness Holds Up

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) reports after the close, with earnings expected at $6.54 per share on $63.34 billion in revenue. Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) is expected to earn 45 cents per share on $28.06 billion.

SpaceX showed that renting out AI capacity can pay. Meta has to show that building it can, too.

news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) reports third-quarter earnings Wednesday after the bell, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg under pressure to show returns on the company’s soaring AI spending.

Analysts expect earnings of $5.89 per share on $63.36 billion in revenue, up nearly 24%. The call begins at 4:30 p.m. ET.

On Kalshi, traders expect plenty of AI discussion, but give just a 1% chance of hearing the name of a company supplying Meta with up to $27 billion in computing capacity.

What Kalshi Predicts Meta Will Say

“Muse” leads at 98%, with at least three mentions required.

Meta’s AI agent has attracted 10.9 million downloads and 2.5 million daily users since September, according to Sensor Tower. But its push into online shopping faces resistance: Amazon blocked Muse from purchasing products on its website.

“Cloud” trades at 93%. Meta is buying computing capacity from specialist providers, including Nebius, while building its own infrastructure.

Meta revealed Monday that its Prometheus supercluster in Ohio is operational, with plans to expand toward one million Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) GPUs.

“Silicon” sits at 74%. Meta is developing four generations of custom AI chips with Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO), aiming to reduce computing costs and reliance on Nvidia.

“Ray-Ban” trades at 70%, versus 36% for “Oakley,” Meta’s newer AI glasses range aimed at athletes.

Both are made by EssilorLuxottica (OTC:ESLOY), which reported Tuesday that wearables revenue grew 20% to €486 million, down from nearly 100% growth the previous quarter.

The figures include Meta’s smart glasses and Nuance hearing devices.

What Kalshi Predicts Meta Will Skip

“Algorithm” trades near 50%, while “Advertising” sits at 40%, despite ads generating $59.4 billion of Meta’s $60.8 billion in second-quarter revenue.

Meta disclosed last week that its new Generative Ads Model improved conversions by 18.9% and click-through rates by 12%. The mention odds reflect the wording of the call, not whether management will discuss its largest business.

“Age Verification” sits at 20%, while “TikTok” trades at 19%.

Meta’s $18 billion settlement with U.S. states imposes tighter age checks and limits on teenage social media use.

The deal ties $5.3 billion of Meta’s payments to TikTok and YouTube adopting similar protections and making matching payments. Meta also expects a $10 billion legal charge this quarter.

“Hyperion” trades at just 17%. Meta’s planned five-gigawatt Louisiana data center faces growing financing concerns, with the Financial Times reporting that bonds linked to the project have fallen below face value.

“Nebius” sits at 1%, despite Meta’s five-year computing agreement with Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS), worth up to $27 billion.

The deal includes $12 billion in dedicated capacity beginning in 2027, plus up to $15 billion in additional purchases. Meta did not name Nebius on its previous earnings call, suggesting management may discuss infrastructure spending without identifying individual suppliers.

Reading the Board

Meta expects to spend $130 billion to $145 billion on capital expenditures this year, with FactSet analysts projecting $196 billion in 2027.

The spending is already eating into cash flow. Meta generated $31.9 billion in operating cash flow last quarter, but just $784 million remained after capital expenditures.

With Muse gaining users and advertising revenue surging, Zuckerberg must convince investors that Meta’s mounting AI spending will pay off.

Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) handed short sellers a rough morning. The server maker raised its first-quarter revenue outlook by $4 billion at the midpoint late Tuesday and guided gross margins well above its prior range, sending shares sharply higher in Wednesday’s premarket session.

  • SMCI stock is rallying. See the chart and price action here. 

Guidance Moves Higher 

In a preliminary update released after Tuesday’s close, Super Micro said it now expects first-quarter revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, compared with earlier guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. The company credited stronger demand for AI platforms. 

Margins may matter more. Super Micro now sees gross margins of 12% to 12.5%, up from a prior forecast of 10.4% to 10.8%. Thin margins have long been a central criticism of the stock, and the new range marks a meaningful step up from recent guidance. 

Short Interest Sets Up a Squeeze

Bears were heavily positioned heading into the update. Short interest stood at about 87.4 million shares, or 17.63% of the float, as of the Sept. 30 settlement date, according to Benzinga Pro data. 

A crowded short position paired with an upside surprise can force traders to buy back shares, which adds fuel to a rally.

The next short interest report, covering mid-October positions, should show whether bears started covering before the news hit. Data reflecting trading after Tuesday’s update will take longer to arrive.

Read Also: Space Stocks Coast Through SpaceX Q3 Print: Rocket Lab, Firefly Steady

A Volatile Track Record

Skeptics still have reasons for caution as SMCI’s results have swung widely too. Revenue topped estimates by 22.2% in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, then missed by 17.6% in the third quarter. 

Governance questions also linger. Super Micro named former Western Digital Corp. (NASDAQ:WDC) executive Mark Long as CFO last week, nearly two years after launching a search tied to concerns about its financial and accounting practices, Reuters reported. 

Separately, a contractor linked to the company pleaded guilty in a case involving the illegal export of servers containing Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) AI chips to China. 

Super Micro has pointed to earlier statements noting it was not named as a defendant and the case has not affected its business operations, according to Reuters. 

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Analysts Lift Targets

Rosenblatt maintained a Buy rating Wednesday and raised its price target to $57 from $51, according to Benzinga data. Citigroup and Mizuho both hold Neutral ratings, with targets of $45 and $43, respectively.

Super Micro will report full first-quarter results after the close on Nov. 3 and host a conference call at 5 p.m. ET the same day.

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) stock rose Wednesday after an AI server rival raised its revenue outlook and Dell announced new products across its artificial intelligence portfolio.

The gains came as Nasdaq futures rose 0.70%, while S&P 500 futures advanced 0.28%.

Super Micro’s Strong Outlook Signals Robust AI Server Demand

Super Micro Computer Inc. (NASDAQ:SMCI) raised its first-quarter revenue guidance Tuesday after the market closed, signaling strong demand for AI servers.

The company now expects revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, up from its previous forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion.

The sharp increase fueled optimism about AI infrastructure spending and potential demand for Dell’s competing server products.

Dell Expands AI Portfolio, Customer Base Surges

At NVIDIA GTC on Wednesday, Dell announced new products and infrastructure upgrades through its Dell AI Factory platform, developed with NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA).

The updates include deskside solutions for agentic AI and modular infrastructure designed to help businesses deploy AI applications.

Dell also reported that more than 6,500 enterprise customers have adopted its AI Factory platform, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter.

Executive Transactions Draw Attention

Separately, Securities and Exchange Commission filings Monday disclosed stock transactions involving Dell executives and major shareholders.

Chief Accounting Officer Richard Troy Sharp reported that 146 shares were withheld at $507.93 each on Oct. 15 to cover approximately $74,000 in tax obligations tied to restricted stock units.

Sharp retained 6,584 shares following the transaction. The withholding was related to taxes and did not represent an open-market sale.

Separate filings disclosed that three Silver Lake-affiliated funds distributed a combined 51,591 Class C shares to certain employees and managing members.

Dell Technical Analysis

The stock remains below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of $536.95 and its 50-day SMA of $513.37, signaling continued near-term weakness despite Wednesday’s rebound.

It is roughly 8% below its 20-day SMA and 3.8% below its 50-day SMA. A sustained move above these levels could strengthen bullish momentum.

However, the longer-term trend remains positive. The stock trades about 6% above its 100-day SMA of $466.08 and 55.7% above its 200-day SMA of $317.31.

The stock’s March golden cross, when the 50-day SMA moved above the 200-day SMA, also supports the longer-term bullish outlook.

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is in the spotlight this week as its GTC Berlin conference runs Oct. 20 to Oct. 22. The event didn’t lift Nvidia’s stock price much, but one market expert is excited for what’s to come.

Gene Munster on GTC Berlin

GTC Berlin featured several announced partnerships from Nvidia and a keynote from CEO Jensen Huang that highlights the company’s future growth.

"Jensen opens Berlin keynote with the familiar line: Nvidia is an AI factory company, not just GPUs," Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner Gene Munster tweeted.

Munster said Nvidia’s AI factory includes software, libraries, and hardware that form a full stack supporting recurring upgrade cycles.

"My take: still underappreciated by investors."

The investor said this is a "long-term positive for revenue growth" for Nvidia.

Munster highlighted Nvidia’s new DSX Pod, which he said is "basically a mini center in a container the size of a bus." The investor said this could speed up the time it takes to spin up a data center from 5 months to one month, making the return on investment more attractive.

Huang mentioned AI agents like Muse from Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) and Grok Bot from SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), telling the audience that these agents will push token usage "through the roof."

Munster said agents can consume 10-15x the tokens of a chatbot, which should increase compute demand for the next few years as more consumers start using bots daily.

While Huang was positive on the impact AI agents will have on software companies as a sector, Munster disagrees and said some companies in the sector could struggle.

The investor named Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) and Adobe Inc (NASDAQ:ADBE) as software companies that could struggle as AI agents expand.

What’s Next for Nvidia

Munster said Nvidia did not update guidance or share any new financial metrics during Huang’s keynote, noting this may be since the October quarter ends in a week.

"Last night’s $SPCX December quarter capex guide of $35-$40B is a positive read-through for what we should hear from Nvidia on the earnings call in about a month."

Nvidia is expected to report third-quarter financial results in November. Analysts expect earnings per share of $2.48 and revenue of $109.17 billion, according to data from Benzinga Pro. That’s up from $1.30 and $57.01 billion year-over-year.

The company has beaten analyst estimates for earnings per share in 15 straight quarters and beaten revenue estimates in 16 straight quarters.

CrowdStrike Holdings Inc (NASDAQ:CRWD) shares are rising Wednesday. The cybersecurity company teamed up more closely with NVIDIA to guard AI agents. Here’s what you should know.

  • CrowdStrike stock is climbing after announcing a deeper NVIDIA partnership to secure AI agents in software and hardware.

CrowdStrike Expands NVIDIA Collaboration On AI Security

CrowdStrike and NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) unveiled a plan at GTC 2026 for watching autonomous AI agents at two levels: the software they run on and the hardware beneath.

The deal builds on Nvidia’s new OpenShell Reference Architecture. CrowdStrike has plugged Falcon Guardian, its AI Detection and Response (AIDR) product, into OpenShell, a secure runtime from Nvidia. A second tie-up with Nvidia Sentry, which enforces policy in the chip itself, is still planned.

Plugging into OpenShell gives Falcon a view of what agents are told, how models answer and what runs afterward. Falcon then checks that activity against the rest of its security data, which helps enterprises catch malicious behavior in agent workflows.

Sentry adds a deeper layer. Planned to run on BlueField-4 DPUs, it would pair AIDR with monitoring done outside the main system and with policy rules enforced in the chip. That gives enterprises a way to detect and contain risky agent behavior the software layer misses.

Executives Back the Approach

CrowdStrike chief business officer Daniel Bernard argues that AI agents have created a fresh attack surface and that “guardrails alone won’t stop an adversary.” Bernard says partnering with Nvidia lets CrowdStrike set the standard for securing autonomous AI.

Autodesk also backed the approach. Chief trust officer Sebastian Goodwin said Autodesk’s customers build structures, products and infrastructure where mistakes are costly, so Autodesk expects the same rigor from its AI agents. With Falcon Guardian, Autodesk can monitor its agents’ actions and access and decide when to step in. Deeper infrastructure controls, Goodwin said, will help customers of all sizes trust their AI.

Nvidia vice president of enterprise Justin Boitano said protection has to reach from the runtime to the infrastructure underneath once agents go into production. OpenShell supplies the base for runtime security and hardware enforcement, Boitano said, and the two companies are working to deliver it at scale.

CRWD Shares Are Rising

CRWD Price Action: CrowdStrike shares were up 4.17% at $236.85 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro.

CrowdStrike crossed above its 50-day moving average of $233.79 on Wednesday. The stock is above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, but still below its 20-day moving average ($256.37), suggesting the shorter-term trend has been weaker than the longer-term setup.
